The block is a redstone signal source that uses the output stored with
`world.set-block-redstone-output` (and its face variant). Redstone wire connects to it
and repeaters, torches and neighbouring blocks read its power. Nothing is stored to
start with, so the block gives no power until the plugin stores some. The output is
kept in memory only and dropped when the block is replaced or moved: store it again
after a restart. Without stored output this flag asks for no event, use `weak-power` and
`strong-power` for that.

Redstone readers ask for the weak power of the block with a
`custom-block-redstone-power-event` whose `strong` is false, unless output is stored for
the block. Makes the block a redstone signal source, like `redstone-output`. Runs
whenever redstone looks at the block, handle it very quickly.

Redstone readers ask for the strong power of the block with a
`custom-block-redstone-power-event` whose `strong` is true, unless output is stored for
the block. Makes the block a redstone signal source, like `redstone-output`. Runs
whenever redstone looks at the block, handle it very quickly.

Comparators can read the block: from the analog output stored with
`world.set-block-comparator-output`, else with a `custom-block-comparator-output-event`.
The output that is stored is kept in memory only and dropped when the block is replaced
or moved. Placing the block updates the comparators next to it.

The shape of the block depends on more than its state, like a copycat that takes the
shape of another block: the server asks with a `custom-block-shape-event` for the
collision, selection and visual shape. The answer is cached per position, so call
`world.invalidate-block-shape` whenever it would change. Placing or removing the block
clears it on its own. The registered shapes are the start of the event's list.

A player right clicks the block with an empty hand: `custom-block-use-event` with
`with-item` false.

A player right clicks the block holding an item: `custom-block-use-event` with

A player left clicks the block (starts digging): `custom-block-attack-event`.
A player picks the block (middle click): `custom-block-clone-item-event` sets the item.

A player is about to break the block: `custom-block-player-will-destroy-event`, which

The friction (slipperiness, 0.6 for most blocks) of the block comes from a

The speed factor (1.0 normally) comes from a `custom-block-physics-event` with kind

The jump factor (1.0 normally) comes from a `custom-block-physics-event` with kind

Each numeric level corresponds to a specific role:
- `Zero`: `normal`: Player can use basic commands.

- `Three`:  `admin`: Player or executor can use commands related to multiplayer management.
- `Four`: `owner`: Player or executor can use all of the commands, including commands related to server management.

Common interface for registering and querying recipes.

The queries are read only and cover the vanilla recipes, the recipes of datapacks, the
recipes added with the register functions below and the recipes of plugin defined types.
Furnaces and the crafting table of the server use the vanilla recipes (and, for crafting,
the dynamic ones), a cooking recipe added by a plugin is reported by the queries only.

Recipes of plugin defined types are plugin side data. They are not synchronised to
clients (the recipe book only knows the vanilla recipe displays), they are kept apart from
datapack recipes, so a datapack reload does not remove them, and they are never removed or
changed. Registering needs the `registry.recipes` permission.

Datapack crafting, cooking, stonecutting and smithing (transform and trim) recipes are
loaded, `find-recipes` and `get-recipe-by-id` return them. A datapack reload replaces the
datapack recipes, the ones plugins registered with `register-shaped`,
`register-shapeless` and `register-cooking` are kept and applied again.
